as_written_in_papers.quote: Genetic testing identified a hemizygous LAMP2 mutation (c.865-2A>G, exon 7, NM_002294), affecting splicing (Figure 2A)

cases.statement: Proband II-1, an 18-year-old hemizygous man with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, pre-excitation and elevated CK, who died 12 years later. His heterozygous mother (not in the batch) later developed cardiomegaly and heart failure. The abstract says 3 of his children also carry the variant; his 3 daughters were later diagnosed with Danon disease, his son was not (individual genotypes of the children not given in the text).

phenotype_specificity.statement: Classic male presentation as described by the authors (hypertrophy, pre-excitation, elevated CK, cardiomyocyte glycogen vacuoles). Authors state the work-up considered amyloidosis, PRKAG2 syndrome and Fabry disease; the genes tested and their results are not reported.

quotes.quote: After confirming the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy phenotype, evaluation focused on storage diseases (light chain and transthyretin amyloidosis, PRKAG2 syndrome, Fabry disease, Anderson-Fabry disease) and common genetic causes.
Histopathology revealed cardiomyocytes with glycogen inclusions and cytoplasmic vacuoles (Figures 4A to 4C).

Young men exhibiting myocardial hypertrophy, elevated plasma creatine kinase, pre-excitation on electrocardiography, and/or characteristic late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance should be evaluated for Danon disease.

segregation.statement: Affected heterozygous mother (cardiomegaly, heart failure, sudden death); father negative. Abstract: 3 children also carry the variant; 3 daughters later diagnosed with Danon disease, son not diagnosed. Which children were tested positive is not stated beyond '3 children'.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo in the proband: the variant was found in his mother (maternally inherited). Whether the mother's variant arose de novo is not reported.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: From the batch HGVS, c.865-2A>G is at position -2 of the intron acceptor site preceding c.865 (exon 7 per the authors); protein effect p.? (not tested in the paper). Authors say it affects splicing and describe the disease as caused by loss-of-function variants.

quotes.quote: Genetic testing identified a hemizygous LAMP2 mutation (c.865-2A>G, exon 7, NM_002294), affecting splicing (Figure 2A)
Danon disease is a rare X-linked dominant disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in lysosome-associated membrane protein-2 (LAMP2).

authors_classification.statement: Authors classify as pathogenic under ACMG with PVS1+PS2+PS4+PM2.

quotes.quote: classified as pathogenic according to American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics guidelines (PVS1+PS2+PS4+PM2)

concerns: Internal contradiction: the authors cite a de novo criterion code in their classification, yet the paper reports the variant in the proband's heterozygous mother (maternally inherited).

Carriers missing from the batch: the heterozygous affected mother (extracted as 'mother of II-1' with a variant row) and the 3 children said in the abstract to carry the variant (no variant rows extracted). Only II-1 is in the batch.
The splicing statement cites 'Figure 2A', which is an echocardiography panel; no splicing assay is described in the text.
Transcript given without version (NM_002294); the batch uses NM_002294.3. Exon 7 numbering stated by authors.
Contradiction on family history: the proband 'denied any family history', but his mother was later diagnosed with heart failure and carried the variant.
Children: the abstract says 3 children carry the variant, while the outcome section says the 3 daughters were diagnosed and the son was not; which children were genotyped is not stated per child.
notes_for_panel: Male hemizygous proband with maternally inherited variant and transmission to affected daughters; family pedigree in Figure 5 (not available as text).
